short: Germany's direct answer to the T-34, and the best-balanced tank it built.
full:
The Panther was ordered after German officers examined captured T-34s in 1941; MAN's design borrowed the sloped armour and wide tracks while keeping German transmission and optics. Production began in January 1943 and the tank went straight to Kursk in July, where many of the 200 committed broke down or caught fire before they could be used properly. The 7.5 cm KwK 42 L/70 had a higher muzzle velocity than the Tiger's 88 and could penetrate any Allied tank it was likely to meet.

The Ausf. A and Ausf. G versions corrected most of the early faults, though final drives remained fragile and the tank was always short of trained crews and fuel. About 6,000 were built. In Normandy and the Ardennes it was the most dangerous German tank in general service, and after the war France operated captured Panthers in the 503rd Armoured Regiment while it rebuilt its own industry.
